question: Do the junctions of the break-shape eddies with W = y^2(1 + y) fall into finitely many kinds with a fixed transfer matrix (each junction shared 1/p among its parents), and if not, can ancestry carry c(t) = c(t - 2) + c(t - 3) as a matching or as a native spine of interval types?

public_inputs.run: scripts/longrun.py launch job.py; python3 -B merge.py <out dir> <results.json>
public_inputs.reused: LOOP-CATALOGUE eddy.py (growth), catalogue.json; BREAK-EDDIES population.json and posthoc_full.json (the corrected W table)

forbidden_inputs: Changing a start, a window, a type list or a prediction after reading any frozen growth
cheapest_meaningful_control: the Q starts (same rate, another W) and the catalogue's five eddies (the cover's exact transfer)

predictions.J1: distinct out-shares per round rise across the window's thirds in all 30
predictions.J2: sum-equitable kinds per round rise across the thirds in all 30
predictions.J3: T: perfect spine matching at lags (2, 3) at every round from 4 with the recurrence holding; C: a matching saturating the smaller side at every round past the lags
predictions.J4: no set of up to 3 of the 10 most frequent interval types is biregular on both halves in any T start
predictions.J5: T: d = 0 from round 4; Q: d not identically 0 and d(t) = -d(t-2) - d(t-3) from round 9

decision_rules.each: held iff no exception, scored by merge.py

stop_rule: One run; read-out; referee hand-off; report.
disclosed_exploration: pilot on population index 28 and the catalogue's five (pilot/)
